learning_outcomes.text: Understand the fundamental principles of physics and their applications in problematic situations. Specifically: a. enunciate the principles; b. indicate the relationships between principles; c. compare explanations of the same phenomenon or situation using different principles.
Know the main laws that explain physical phenomena. Specifically: a. illustrate the law in mathematical terms; b. evaluate the limits of the law; c. extend the law to similar and unknown situations.

Know physical quantities operationally, indicating the correct units of measurement. Specifically: a. define fundamental quantities; b. know the operations between fundamental quantities; c. describe derived quantities in terms of fundamental quantities.

Know the field of inquiry of physics. Specifically: a. understand the physical meaning of the mathematical entities used to describe phenomena; b. delineate the field of applicability (macroscopic/microscopic) of the laws used to describe phenomena; c. describe the investigation methods used in physics.
Analyze and examine proposed physical situations by formulating explanatory hypotheses through mathematical models, analogies, or physical laws.

Formalize problematic situations and apply the concepts explained in the course, mathematical methods, and disciplinary tools learned during the course and relevant to their resolution, performing, where necessary, calculations, estimations, and qualitative reasoning.

Interpret and/or elaborate proposed and/or derived data, including experimental data, verifying their relevance to the chosen model and representing them, where necessary, using graphical-symbolic language.
Argue and describe solution strategies adopted in problematic physical situations, communicating the results obtained while evaluating their consistency with the proposed problematic situation.

syllabus_topics: The Scientific Method
Physical quantities and their operational definition, units of measurement, dimensions
Kinematics of a material point in one dimension
Vector quantities and kinematics of a point in multiple dimensions
Parabolic motion of bodies and circular motion
Inertial reference frames, definition of force and mass
Principles of dynamics
Fundamental forces and force laws
Contact forces, constraint forces, empirical force laws (elastic force, friction and viscous forces)
Notable problems: inclined plane, harmonic oscillator, simple pendulum
Impulse and momentum
Work and kinetic energy
Conservative forces and potential energy
Conservation of mechanical energy and momentum
Collisions in one dimension
Angular momentum and moment of forces
Relative motions, non-inertial reference frames and the concept of apparent force
Notes on the motion of planets in the solar system
Dynamics of systems of material points: cardinal equations, center of mass, conservation laws, Koenig's theorem for kinetic energy
Elements of rigid body dynamics, rotations about a fixed axis
Elements of fluid statics and dynamics
Temperature and heat, first principle of thermodynamics
Ideal gases
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written and an oral part. The written test includes multiple-choice questions, free-response questions, and numerical exercises.
